title: RTEC Title VI complaint correspondence templates
lifecycle: Acknowledgement template confirms receipt, identifies the allegation, states that an investigation will begin, and invites additional information/questions.
Substantiated template states that apparent Title VI violation(s) were identified and that corrective efforts are underway; it anticipates possible further administrative-hearing contact.
Not-substantiated template explains that no Title VI violation/evidence of civil-rights-law noncompliance was found, closes the matter, and provides reconsideration/external-filing language.

currentness_conflict.finding: The not-substantiated template gives seven calendar days to provide additional information for reconsideration.
currentness_conflict.current_plan: The January 2026 Board-approved Title VI/LEP plan gives 90 days after the closure/Letter of Finding date to appeal.
currentness_conflict.risk: A current-looking template names the current 2026 coordinator but carries a shorter historical reconsideration period. It should not be used operationally until reconciled with the approved plan.
currentness_conflict.required_action: Revise/approve the template set so acknowledgement, closure/finding, reconsideration/appeal language and coordinator/contact information match the current approved Title VI plan.

controls: Template/version IDs should be tied to the governing Title VI plan version.
Case-specific names, allegations, investigative facts and correspondence remain restricted records.
Do not infer a substantiated or unsubstantiated outcome from the existence of a blank template.
